data.name: StandardizeStep_StandardFolders_Title
data.value: Move files to the standard folders (OEBPS/Text, Styles, Images…)

data.name: StandardizeStep_StandardFolders_Description
data.value: Every file goes to the folder for its type, and all references to it are updated.

data.name: StandardizeStep_StandardFolders_Info
data.value:
What it does: • Moves every file to the standard folder for its type: – HTML/XHTML → OEBPS/Text – CSS → OEBPS/Styles – images → OEBPS/Images – fonts → OEBPS/Fonts – audio → OEBPS/Audio, video → OEBPS/Video – everything else (e.g. JS, XML) → OEBPS/Misc – the OPF and the NCX → OEBPS • Renames the OPF to content.opf and the NCX to toc.ncx. • When two files in different folders have the same name (ignoring case), the second one gets a unique numbered name, e.g. main.css → main0001.css. • Updates every reference to the moved files: href/src in HTML, url(…) in CSS, the OPF and NCX entries and META-INF/container.xml.
Example: text/part0001.html → OEBPS/Text/part0001.html, stylesheet.css → OEBPS/Styles/stylesheet.css.
It does not change the file contents (apart from references) or the extensions. Renaming a file (the OPF, the NCX, name collisions) also changes its manifest ID.

data.name: StandardizeStep_StandardFileExtensions_Description
data.value: Every file gets the extension of its type, e.g. an XHTML chapter saved as .html becomes .xhtml.

data.name: StandardizeStep_StandardFileExtensions_Summary
data.value: Files to get a new extension: {0}.

data.name: StandardizeStep_StandardFileExtensions_Info
data.value:
What it does: • Every file whose extension does not match its MIME type gets the standard extension for that type. The folder stays the same. – XHTML (also text/html) → .xhtml, e.g. part0001.html → part0001.xhtml – JPEG → .jpg, e.g. cover.jpeg → cover.jpg – CSS → .css, e.g. style.txt → style.css • When the new name is already taken in the same folder, the file gets a unique numbered name instead — nothing is overwritten. • Updates every reference to the renamed files (HTML, CSS, OPF, NCX). • Renaming a file also changes its manifest ID (e.g. ch01 → ch01.xhtml).
It does not change the file contents (apart from references) or the folders.

data.name: StandardizeStep_RebaseManifestIds_Title
data.value: Base OPF manifest IDs on file names

data.name: StandardizeStep_RebaseManifestIds_Description
data.value: Every manifest entry gets an ID made from its file name, e.g. id12 → part0001_xhtml.

data.name: StandardizeStep_RebaseManifestIds_Info
data.value:
What it does: • Gives every OPF manifest entry an ID made from its file name: – the dot before the extension becomes an underscore: part0001.xhtml → part0001_xhtml – accented letters become plain ASCII: chapitré.xhtml → chapitre_xhtml – an ID starting with a digit gets an "x" prefix: 00008.jpeg → x00008_jpeg • When that ID is already taken, a number is appended, e.g. part0001_xhtml0001. • Updates every reference to the changed IDs in the OPF: the spine (itemref idref), the toc attribute, the cover meta, refines, media-overlay and fallback.
Example: <item id="id12" href="Text/part0001.xhtml"> → <item id="part0001_xhtml" …>.
It does not change the files or their names. The IDs are based on the file names after the operations above.

data.name: StandardizeStep_ManifestMediaTypes_Description
data.value: Manifest entries with an empty or unknown MIME type get the type Signet recognised.

data.name: StandardizeStep_ManifestMediaTypes_Info
data.value:
What it does: • Compares the media-type of every OPF manifest entry with the type Signet loaded the file with, and fixes the entries that differ. • This affects entries with an empty or unknown MIME type — when loading the book, Signet recognised their type from the file extension.
Example: <item href="Styles/style.css" media-type="application/octet-stream"> → media-type="text/css".
It does not change the files, their names or their IDs.
